key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: SUDDEN onset within hours to days. LOCATION: UNILATERAL or bilateral kidney involvement. DURATION: Develops over hours to days, may persist for days to weeks. CHARACTER: SEVERE flank pain, fever, chills. AGGRAVATING: MOVEMENT, urination. RELIEVING: ANTIBIOTICS, pain medications. TIMING: Sudden onset, develops over hours to days. SEVERITY: 7-9/10, severe and unrelenting. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: SEVERE FLANK PAIN, fever, chills, nausea, vomiting, may have hematuria. KEY POSITIVES: Severe flank pain, fever, chills, positive urinalysis, positive blood cultures. KEY NEGATIVES: No neck stiffness, no focal neurological deficits.

red_flags: High fever with rigors - possible sepsis, call 911
Signs of severe infection - fever, chills, rigors - call 911
Severe hypertension with neurological deficits - possible hypertensive crisis, call 911
Signs of severe metabolic acidosis - deep breathing, confusion, coma - call 911
Signs of severe electrolyte imbalances - confusion, seizures, cardiac arrhythmias - call 911
